validated_results.title: Serum phytoestrogens and prostate cancer risk in a nested case-control study among Japanese men.
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within a Japanese cohort reporting an odds ratio for incident prostate cancer by serum genistein concentration, a target-specific human biomarker exposure estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest serum genistein level
extraction.population: Male participants of the Japan Collaborative Cohort (JACC) Study who donated sera

sample_size.excerpt: Three datasets were analyzed; 1) all subjects, 2) 40 cases and 101 controls after excluding subjects with low testosterone levels who were suspected of having had medical intervention, and 3) 28 cases and 69 controls with prostate specific antigen level of </= 10.0 ng/ml.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 40 + 101 = 141

cases.excerpt: Three datasets were analyzed; 1) all subjects, 2) 40 cases and 101 controls after excluding subjects with low testosterone levels who were suspected of having had medical intervention, and 3) 28 cases and 69 controls with prostate specific antigen level of </= 10.0 ng/ml.

effect_size.excerpt: The odds ratio (OR) for the highest level to the lowest was 0.38 (95% confidence interval (CI); 0.13, 1.13) for genistein, 0.41 (0.15, 1.11) for daidzein, and 0.34 (0.11, 1.10) for equol for the second dataset.
